newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Weak mark to stimulate Bulgaria exports - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Weak mark to stimulate Bulgaria exports - analysts.

text.p: Bulgaria's currency board system anchoring the lev to the mark means exporters will benefit from the German currency's weakness against the dollar, analysts said on Tuesday.

"The current depreciation of the mark against the dollar will benefit Bulgarian exporters and will curb imports in the short term," said Tatiana Hubenova, an analyst at the Economy Institute of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences.
Bulgaria introduced the IMF-prescribed currency board system on July 1, pegging the lev at 1,000 to the mark.

The mechanism requires that all levs in circulation, bank deposits and current accounts be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves and bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
The mark traded near 1.83 per dollar on global markets on Tuesday, down from around 1.75 on July 1.

"If the lev was overvalued (against the mark) at the time of introduction of the currency board, the current fall in the mark against the dollar would correct the imbalance," Hubenova told a news conference.
Bulgaria's exports are directed mainly to dollar-based markets like Russia and the Arab countries, while imports are mostly linked to mark-dominated European markets like Germany, experts said.

"If the mark fall continues at the same rate it could create a strong inflationary impulse in October and November when dollar-denominated imports of fuels mainly from Russia would increase," said Emil Harsev, owner of Harsev & Co financial consultancy.
If Bulgaria had pegged the lev to a very strong currency like the dollar it would have minimised the chance of economic growth, Hubenova added.
Bulgaria's monthly inflation has steadily declined to 0.8 percent in June from 243 percent in February.
Economists forecast monthly inflation of near four percent in July and August because of a 7.06 percent rise in natural gas prices from August 1.
Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund in April, Bulgaria pledged to slow monthly inflation to two percent by the end of this year.
